$comment: Machine-readable game rights ledger. Issue #609 owns the gate; issue #855 §E owns the
current unified decision that every real game in the shipped catalog carries.
What this file does and does not say:
* scopes.*.boundaries and mode_restrictions are operating ceilings for an approved title,
not a second copy of the approval itself.
* A rights approval never makes data trainable. games.approved_for_trainable, the exact
catalog version, the executable allowlist, object integrity and QA still decide, and the
* runtime_anti_cheat_gate_still_required is an independent red line. No rights decision
satisfies it, and widening rights never weakens it.
Where app_id comes from: for titles whose catalog bundle pins a Steam identity, the app_id is
the one already recorded in this repository (docs/18, docs/40, docs/41, docs/73, docs/74,
The twelve `-pc` catalogs deliberately discover their game by process name and pin no store
identity (docs/143 §1, docs/144 §1), so their app_id identifies the *title* on Steam and the
link to catalog configuration is catalog_game_ids, never the app_id.
status_note: Every real game in the shipped catalog carries the same unified decision. For any record that is not an approval, mode_restrictions are requested technical ceilings, not permissions or publisher-accepted terms.

unified_rights_decision.note: issue #855 §6/§E records the owner and counsel decision as an already-settled input: no extra rights limits beyond the existing technical and safety boundaries, and one identical set of boundaries for every real game rather than per-title or per-publisher rules. It retires the narrower project_research_only lane, whose noncommercial/no-delivery ceilings directly contradict it; the two policies must never be active at the same time. The written counsel document has not been issued yet, so every evidence_url is still empty and is backfilled later for traceability (issue #855 §E.1) rather than as a precondition for the gate.

instrumentation.boundaries: Approved within the existing technical and safety boundaries: local user-mode graphics instrumentation of the bound game process only. Kernel-mode components, protection bypass and anti-cheat interaction stay prohibited, and the runtime anti-cheat gate is enforced separately from this approval.

capture.boundaries: Approved within the existing technical and safety boundaries: capture of the bound game window's video, depth, projection, camera/player pose, input and audio streams and the artifacts derived from them.

commercial_ml.boundaries: Approved within the existing technical and safety boundaries: commercial machine-learning training and evaluation on the captured and derived data. Whether an individual clip may enter a training set is still decided by clip_trainability, not by this approval.

delivery.boundaries: Approved within the existing technical and safety boundaries: delivery of derived datasets and evidence packages to named recipients. Game executables, source code and standalone game assets are never redistributed.

records.mode_restrictions: The runtime anti-cheat gate is still required and is enforced independently of this rights decision: use only the officially supported offline/single-player mode or a publisher-documented anti-cheat-disabled launch mode, and stop immediately if an anti-cheat module, driver or service is active or the approved launch mode drifts. No protection bypass, no mod loader, no multiplayer or matchmaking interaction, and no redistribution of game executables or standalone assets. Single-player offline/local launch only; game and launcher background networking is observed but never blocked or emulated.
records.note: effective_date is the effective date of the unified rights decision itself, not the date on which this project started capturing this title. expiry_or_review_date is a project-set five-year planned review date, not an expiry stated in a counsel document; if that review is not completed in time the existing rights gate blocks fail-closed on its own.
